# Candidate Show HN post

Title: Show HN: Riff – An iPhone calendar you zoom instead of switching views
Project URL: https://riffcalendar.com
Posted (UTC): 2026-10-21T16:25:02Z

## Project page text (fetch status: ok)

```text
Tyler Hall
Building Mac apps since 2006
On Mastodon,
2 September 2026
This is seriously impressive. It’s rare to find such a well-done new
take on an established category like calendar apps.
A closer look
Create an event by holding its time
Hold an empty slot and a new event appears there. Slide to adjust
the start, and drag the bar at its foot to set the duration. For an
all-day event, hold under the date.
Round times by default, exact when needed
Drags snap to round times. For an exact time, pause before you drag
on, or drag the time tag at the left edge.
Riff remembers your regular events
Type the start of a title you have used before, and Riff suggests the
event with its length, place and alert from last time. There is
nothing to set up. The suggestions come from your own calendar.
Reschedule with your calendar in view
Tap the arrows beside an event’s time and it lifts off. Scroll to
another week or day, then place it among what is already there.
The weather where you plan
Each day’s forecast stands beside its date, and a single day shows it
hour by hour. An event pinned to a place shows the forecast
there. Weather is a switch in Riff’s settings.
See when it gets dark
A faint shade covers the hours between sunset and sunrise where you
are, so an evening run before dark is easy to plan. Daylight is a
switch in Riff’s settings.
And there is more: reminders beside your events, search by
title or place, alerts in a tap, time zones when you travel, a one-thumb
zoom…
The calendar itself, as a widget
The Schedule widget is the calendar itself: every event drawn at
its hour, with its length and its name. Each size shows as many days
as you choose, up to three on the small, a week on the medium and two
whole weeks on the large. Month draws this month, or this month and
the next, and Up next lists what is coming, on the Home Screen or the
Lock Screen.
Three days at true scale on the large widget, the day’s list on the medium.
Your calendars, not copies of them
Work
Personal
Family
Riff works directly on the calendars already on your iPhone: iCloud,
Google, Exchange, whatever Apple Calendar sees. There is no Riff account
and nothing to import. Events you create or move in Riff show up
everywhere else. Delete the app and your data hasn’t gone anywhere.
Data collected: none
Riff has no server, no account and no analytics. Your events pass
between Apple’s calendar database and your screen. Riff adds no stop of
its own. Not collecting data isn’t a policy. There is nowhere for it
to go.
Get Riff
★★★★★
The best interface for a calendar app I have yet found. Zooming in
and out is smooth and adding events is a breeze. I actually like to
add more events to my calendar now.
Ashlyme, in an App Store review
Get Riff on the App Store
iPhone · iOS 26 or later
Leave your address for an email when Riff gets a major update.
Email address
Email me about updates
```

## HN discussion (1 comment)

- [other] cavo2000: I've been using Riff for a little while during late testing stage. It takes a little to get used to but moving around the calendar is a lot like Google/Apple Maps. Recurring meetings, which are not exact, like getting a haircut is very easy to book with just one small swipe. The best feature is how quickly you can see an overview. Just like maps.
{"decision": "push", "reason": "Riff 提供了一个有新意的日历交互切入点：用缩放代替切换视图、长按空档直接建事件，并且不需要账户和服务器、直接读写系统日历。页面描述具体，包含天气、日落阴影、小组件等可识别的功能，HN 评论也给出了使用体验，符合小而有巧思的产品标准。"}

verdict.reasoning: Every claim in the reason matches the evidence: zoom in place of view switching, hold an empty slot to create an event, no account or server, works directly on the system calendars, weather, the sunset shading, widgets, and an HN comment describing use. It names concrete features and argues for push, which is the stated decision.
